blocks.text: Chicken Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Whether a specific parcel is in the ALR, its zoning, servicing and floodplain position, and its municipal or rural tax schedule are not verified at parcel level — each is a per-parcel check with the applicable local government, BC Assessment and title.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Municipal layer: a Mission-ground parcel runs on the Mission frame — the City of Mission penalty is FLAT 10% on unpaid taxes after July 2, kept strictly separate from the FVRD rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11: 5% after July 2 + 5% after October 31), and tax follows the jurisdiction of the specific parcel; Mission has NO BC Supreme Court registry (registry mapping not verified). The parcel's own municipality governs; confirm there.

faq.q: Does a chicken coop on a hobby property give it farm value?
faq.a: Value a hobby property as residential/hobby land unless the contract and the board confirm a commercial position.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in this area?
faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.

faq.q: What is the ALR and does it apply to farms in this area?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.
